# Bench

**Class** · `ironwood.bench.Bench`

```java
public class Bench
```

Measures latency in nanoseconds, with warmup exclusion and percentile reports.



Call [`mark()`](#member-mark-28--29-) before an operation and [`measure()`](#member-measure-28--29-) afterward,
or supply an elapsed duration to [`measure(long)`](#member-measure-28-long-29-). Iterations include
warmup; measurements and statistics exclude it. A mark is consumed once.
Instances are intended for one thread and do not synchronize.



The histogram retains one primitive counter per distinct duration. Recording
an existing duration allocates nothing. New durations can grow the histogram
storage. Reset retains that storage for reuse. Percentile reporting sorts
distinct durations and computes the average and maximum of the fastest
rounded fraction of measurements, including part of a repeated duration.
The reported fractions are 75%, 90%, 99%, 99.9%, 99.99%, and 99.999%.



Durations supplied by the caller must be nonnegative, and iteration counts,
measurement counts, and the sum of measured nanoseconds must fit in a signed
long. These caller obligations are not checked on the recording path.
Warmup primes caches and storage in native code; there is no JIT compilation.



Free the benchmark after use to reclaim its histogram and counters.
`results()` returns an independent String that the caller must free;
`printResults()` handles its own temporary report. Reports use comma
grouping, a decimal point, and three fractional digits, regardless of locale.



```java
import ironwood.bench.Bench;

public class BenchExample {

    public static int main(String[] args) {

        Bench bench = new Bench(1);
        bench.measure(1000); // Warmup is ignored.
        bench.measure(10);
        bench.measure(11);
        bench.printResults(); // Average: 10.500 nanos.
        free bench;
        return 0;
    }
}
```

<a name="member-Bench-28-long-2c-boolean-2c-int-29-"></a>

### `Bench(long,boolean,int)`

```java
public Bench(long warmup, boolean verbose, int verboseLogEvery)
```

Creates a benchmark with explicit native logging options.



Logging prints the first iteration and every `verboseLogEvery`
iterations, including warmup. Console output affects subsequent timings.
No system properties or environment variables are consulted.

**Parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `warmup` | the warmup count; nonpositive values disable warmup |
| `verbose` | whether to print progress |
| `verboseLogEvery` | the positive progress interval |

**Throws**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| [`IllegalArgumentException`](../lang/IllegalArgumentException.md) | if the interval is not positive |
